The listening log

Changelog
with receipts.

A short, honest record of what changed—and what got better when we listened harder.

SEP 12, 2026
v0.2.0 · MEASURED MODEL LAB

Measure first. Then make it yours.

The Windows console now keeps raw response, target, and correction visibly separate. Import rig and target metadata, inspect the correction curve, apply a headroom-safe six-band landing, and export an audit trail without modifying the source measurement.

Raw / target / correctionHeadroom safeAudit export
SEP 10, 2026
v0.1.3 · LISTENING PROFILES

Hot-mod it. Save it. Follow it.

The console now saves the complete listening state on this device: EQ bands, output path, headphone controls, preamp, safety ceiling, and bypass. Name a sound, reapply it later, or remove it when it has served its purpose.

Live adjustmentsSaved profilesLocal only
SEP 10, 2026
v0.1.2 · PROFILE LAB

Measurements get a safe landing

The preview accepts a documented getEQd profile JSON, validates the frequency and gain arrays, stores imports locally, and maps correction data into the six-band console for auditioning. The original measurement stays untouched.

Local profile storageCalibration importJSON template
SEP 10, 2026
v0.1.1 · HEADPHONE PASS

Headphones enter the room

The console now has a dedicated headphone path for modern PC listening: 3.5 mm, USB DACs, USB headsets, and Bluetooth. Choose a neutral, closed-back, open-back, or gaming-headset target, then tune crossfeed and stage width without touching your speaker profile.

Headphone targetsCrossfeedStage widthSpatial handoff
SEP 10, 2026
v0.1.0 · PREVIEW

The first hit

getEQd arrives with a six-band response curve tuned for real listening: sub-kick control, low-mid cleanup, presence shaping, and a gentle air shelf. The console now supports Reference, Impact, Dialogue, and Night profiles.

6-band EQ5.1 outputLimiter
NEXT UP
v0.3.0 · ROADMAP

The system-wide handoff

Next comes the larger Windows integration: an APO or virtual-driver path that can follow other applications while preserving output routing, channel intent, and signing requirements.

System-wide engineOutput routingSigned integration
ALWAYS
THE RULE

Trust your ears

Every control gets a label, a useful range, and a reason to exist. If a feature cannot make the next listening session better, it can wait.
